text: dsh-kernel-mesh 是一款面向 DSH 的模型路由与子代理插件，将 Kimi、Grok、Codex 和 MiniMax 的模型适配器注册到会话模型选择中，并提供 kernel_status、kernel_switch 与 kernel_run 工具。它还能按内核配方启动后台或前台子代理，并在供应商插件和凭据齐备时提供 Kimi、Grok 搜索与网页抓取。适合希望在 DSH 会话中切换不同编码模型或委派任务的用户；需要相应供应商的本机登录配置。

dsh-kernel-mesh adds Kimi, Grok, Codex, and MiniMax routes to DSH, with tools to inspect and switch routes or delegate tasks to kernel-specific subagents. Optional Kimi and Grok search and fetch tools appear when their plugins and credentials are available. Configure provider logins locally.
想在同一个 DSH 会话里切换 Kimi、Grok、Codex 或 MiniMax 模型。
让 DSH 把独立的编码任务交给 Kimi 或 Grok 子代理后台处理。
我想查看当前有哪些外部模型路由和子代理类型已经注册。
需要把 DSH 后续新会话的默认模型切换到另一家供应商。
想在 DSH 里用 Kimi 或 Grok 搜索网页并抓取页面内容。
How can I switch DSH sessions between Kimi, Grok, Codex, and MiniMax models?
I want DSH to delegate a coding task to a background subagent using another coding harness.
Can DSH search the web with Kimi or Grok and fetch a page as text?
dsh-kernel-mesh 的功能「模型路由」：向 DSH 注册 Kimi、Grok、Codex 和 MiniMax 模型适配器，让用户从模型选择中切换；每条路由依相应本机供应商配置启用。
dsh-kernel-mesh 的功能「跨内核子代理」：调用 kernel_run 按 Kimi、Grok 或 Codex 的配方委派任务，默认后台启动并返回子代理标识，也可选择前台等待结果。
dsh-kernel-mesh 的功能「状态与默认路由」：kernel_status 汇报已注册路由及子代理类型，kernel_switch 则保存后续会话使用的默认模型路由。
dsh-kernel-mesh 的功能「供应商网页搜索」：满足供应商插件和凭据条件时注册 kimi_search、kimi_fetch、grok_search 与 grok_fetch，供模型检索网页或读取页面内容。

dsh-kernel-mesh README · dsh-kernel-mesh：DSH runs on one simple idea: **everything is a plugin**. Models, tools, subagents — plug them together however you like.

So we did exactly that: we turned four coding harnesses — **Kimi Code**, **Grok Build**, **OpenAI Codex**, and **MiniMax Mini-Agent** — into DSH plugins, bundled in this one package.

dsh-kernel-mesh README · dsh-kernel-mesh：The payoff is simple: switch to a Kimi / Grok / Codex / MiniMax model inside DSH, and it's **no different** from opening each one's own CLI. Every model stays in the environment it knows best — main agent or subagent, it feels like coming home.

dsh-kernel-mesh README · What's inside：- **L1 kernel routes** — `kimi-kernel` / `grok-kernel` / `codex-kernel` / `minimax-kernel`, registered as DSH model routes your main agent can switch to.
- **L2 subagent recipes** — `kimi-agent` / `kimi-explore` / `kimi-plan`, `grok-agent` / `grok-explore` / `grok-plan`, `codex-agent` / `codex-explore` / `codex-worker` (each kernel's own subagent types; minimax has none upstream). Each recipe carries the vendor's own subagent prompt and tool whitelist, so a kernel subagent sees and uses exactly what that harness's subagent would — independent of the parent's preset.
- **Three kernel tools** — `kernel_status`, `kernel_run`, `kernel_switch`.
- **Four agent presets** — `codex-kernel`, `grok-kernel`, `kimi-kernel`, and `minimax-kernel` ship in this package's `presets/` directory. Copy them into the official user-preset root (`~/.dsh/.agent-presets/`) to make them appear in the preset picker (the official DSH CLI owns the shipped preset root, so a bundle cannot register extra roots).
- **Vendor search tools, offered only when opted in** — `kimi_search` / `kimi_fetch` appear only if `dsh-kernel-kimi` is installed **and** a Moonshot credential exists

dsh-kernel-mesh README · Kernel matrix：| Kernel | Wire | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kimi-kernel` | Anthropic Messages | `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/messages` (kimi-cli **1.49.0**: `max_tokens` clamped to remaining context; catalog includes `k3`) |
| `grok-kernel` | Responses (proxy) | `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/responses` |
| `codex-kernel` | Responses (custom) | your codex `base_url` + `/responses` |
| `minimax-kernel` | Anthropic Messages (CN) | `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages` |

dsh-kernel-mesh README · System prompts：Each kernel plugin registers the vendor's upstream system prompt (tool names and
runtime placeholders adapted to the DSH tool surface) as the agent's sole
system-prompt section (`complete: true` + `suppressRuntimeContext()`), so a
session on a kernel sees ONLY that harness's prompt — not DSH's.

dsh-kernel-mesh README · Fallback routes (opt-in)：The vendors have no fallback of their own, so by default each kernel uses its
official API. If a kernel's own API is out of quota, set
`DSH_KERNEL_USE_FALLBACK=1` to route the kernels through your existing
subscriptions instead:

| Kernel | Fallback route | Model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kimi-kernel` | ollama | `kimi-k2.7-code` |
| `grok-kernel` | ollama | `gpt-oss:120b` |
| `codex-kernel` | opencode-go | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| `minimax-kernel` | ollama | `minimax-m3` |

dsh-kernel-mesh README · Fallback routes (opt-in)：Keys are read from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` (`OLLAMA_API_KEY`,
`MY_OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`). Leave `DSH_KERNEL_USE_FALLBACK` unset (or `0`) for
the official kernel APIs.

dsh-kernel-mesh README · Install：Install the bundle into your profile with the official plugin command. npm is preferred (prebuilt, no `allowBuilds`):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-kernel-mesh
```

GitHub also works, because this package ships `lib/` in the repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:oppnc/dsh-kernel-mesh
```

dsh-kernel-mesh README · Install：`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm and reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically — this package declares `"dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } }`, so it joins the profile's layer stack. Restart the profile afterwards:

```sh
dsh web
```

Install the kernel surface plugins the presets reference (each is a plain plugin, installed as an inactive dependency and resolved by name from the preset rows):

dsh-kernel-mesh README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-kernel-kimi dsh-kernel-grok dsh-kernel-codex dsh-kernel-minimax
```

Install the four kernel agent presets by copying them from the installed mesh package into the official user-preset root:

```sh
dsh_home="${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}"
cp -r "$dsh_home/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-kernel-mesh/presets/." "$dsh_home/.agent-presets/"
```

Then start a new session and pick the `codex-kernel`, `grok-kernel`, `kimi-kernel`, or `minimax-kernel` preset in the Web UI.

dsh-kernel-mesh README · Usage：```sh
kernel_status                          # which kernels, L2 types, transports are registered
kernel_run(kernel, type, task)         # fan a task out to a foreign kernel
kernel_switch('kimi')                  # set the default model route for future sessions
```

| Kernel | `type` values |
| --- | --- |
| `kimi` | `coder`, `explore`, `plan` |
| `grok` | `general`, `explore`, `plan` |
| `codex` | `explore`, `worker` |
| `minimax` | (none — no subagent tool upstream) |
